S1 BLOCKING — Resume-fork treats a failed checkout as a successfully attached playable fork.
Invariant/authority: ADR 0012 custody and stale-copy fork resolution require the chosen fork to be attached into the campaign slot and acquire custody before the campaign plays that identity; a failed attachment must propagate as failure. The function's own operative contract returns false on an unexpected failure. Owning repair dispatch eshyra-o9bd.19.5.15.3 expressly requires S2's rule across every checkout path, including fork. Effective profile: semantic-system.
Location: packages/cli/src/playFork.ts:78 (ignored checkout result), :85-90 (success narration/true); consumer packages/cli/src/playCharacter.ts:550 and :673.
Concrete scenario: use the same admitted matching unsupported-system state as the repaired custody regressions: campaign binding and registry sheets are pathfinder2e/pf-pack, the campaign copy links pf@1, and the registry head is pf@2. Call forkConflictedCharacterIntoCampaign for source revision 1. It creates fork-pf@1, checkout returns attach.ok:false and transactionally preserves the original campaign sheet, and no fork custody is acquired. Nevertheless the actual CLI helper returns true and tells the player “This campaign now plays the fork.” The real-source/real-SQLite probe reproduced true, localGlobalId pf, null fork custody, and unchanged serialized campaign. In full resume, applyStaleResolution accepts that true and proceeds to acquireCustodyOnResume on the still-stale original, which rejects instead of yielding the chosen resolution.
Boundary/owner and reachability: CLI resume-fork consumption of the public core checkout result. Normal released D&D setup does not create this unsupported-system state; that limits current frequency/consequence, but the public sheet/binding types admit it and this state is expressly within the owning repair and regression scope.
Sibling analysis: ordinary checkoutIntoCampaign checks result.attach.ok; catch-up now throws on false and its CLI consumer catches/reports failure; fork is the other direct checkout consumer and discards the discriminated result. Standalone fork is registry-only and promises no campaign attach. Ordinary acquireCustodyOnResume deliberately does not re-import an already attached copy. The corrected transactional attach makes the failed fork retain the original sheet, so the incorrect consumer assumption has not been repaired by moving it downstream.
Required closure: consume checkout's result in the resume-fork caller; return/report failure on attach.ok:false, with no assertion that the campaign now plays the fork and no continuation into the successful apply path. Preserve campaign copy/custody on failed attach and align any affected inventory claims. No cross-database transaction or rollback of the independently valid registry fork is demanded.
Permanent evidence: a generalized caller failure-result invariant, varying successful checkout, correction result and thrown refusal, should assert success only after the slot adopts the fork and custody is held; failed attachment must preserve campaign/custody and emit failure rather than successful attachment narration. A focused inexpensive real-store caller regression is proportionate to false player-visible identity/state claims.
Repair material: YES (resume control flow and player-visible result semantics).

S2 BLOCKING — The attach capability still declares the pre-repair nontransactional failure behavior.
Invariant/authority: ADR 0020 section 3 requires truthful bounded operation/exclusion declarations; deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts declares itself the authoritative inventory of capabilities in force, and owning DESIGN expressly requires inventory statements to track the repairs. Effective profile: rules-clause-complete for capability claims.
Location: packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityInventory.ts:1699; actual changed mechanism packages/core/src/character/attachCharacter.ts:82-99.
Concrete scenario: attach a matching unsupported-system sheet to a campaign. The inventory says sheet save/import are separate writes and an import correction leaves the saved sheet in place. The new transaction instead rolls back that sheet save and returns ok:false; an existing campaign copy is preserved, or a new attachment leaves no saved sheet. The real-store failed-catch-up regression and exact-source SQLite probe demonstrate the contradiction. The same inventory now makes the opposite, correct claim for checkout (:2308) and catch-up (:2397).
Boundary/owner: maintained internal capability inventory used to assess the bounded implementation. This does not change model-facing presentation directly; its defect is a false in-force persistence guarantee, not a live narration error.
Sibling analysis: compared attach, finalized import, checkout, resume, catch-up, registry and fork statements against producers/consumers, and checkpoint publication, proficiency removal/Expertise, close and narration claims against their mechanisms. The attach helper's own entry was missed when updating its custody callers. Finalized import remains independently transactional and its entry is consistent. Checkpoint comments still use “rename” in places but their no-clobber/atomic property matches hard-link publication; that terminology alone is not another substantive finding.
Required closure: update character-sheet-attach-v1 to state that sheet persistence and live projection share a transaction, a correction result rolls back campaign writes, and thrown import failure also leaves the campaign attachment unchanged. Reconcile related capability statements around that same failure boundary.
Permanent evidence: the existing real-store failed-catch-up rollback regression, checkout evidence and bounded inspection of the corrected declaration suffice; no dedicated prose snapshot, new audit framework or additional expensive proof mechanism is required.
Repair material: NO if confined to correcting the inventory declaration; YES if runtime behavior is changed instead.
